# Goal

Source: https://github.com/wrnrlr/goal-mirror/blob/master/README.md

# Goal

Goal is an embeddable array programming language with a bytecode interpreter,
written in Go. The command line intepreter can execute scripts or run in
interactive mode. Goal shines the most in common scripting tasks, like handling
columnar data or text processing. It is also suitable for exploratory
programming.

# Install

To install the command line interpreter, you only need to have the [go
compiler](https://golang.org/) installed (Go 1.22 or later required). There are
no extra dependencies.

You can then build the intepreter with:

	go build ./cmd/goal

You should now have a working `goal` executable in the current directory. Use
the `--help` option for command-line usage.

Running `goal` without arguments opens the REPL. For a better experience using
the REPL with the usual keyboard shortcuts, you can install the readline
wrapper `rlwrap` program and then use instead `rlwrap goal`. The `rlwrap`
program is available as a package on most systems.

*SIMD optimization.* On amd64, various operations will use vectorized SIMD
assembly implementations by default, requiring SSE CPU extensions up to SSE4.2,
representing a subset of the available instructions when
[GOAMD64](https://go.dev/wiki/MinimumRequirements#amd64) is set to `v2`.  You
may disable those optimizations by passing the `-tags nosse4` option to the
build command.

*Extensions.* The default build only includes the `os` extension package. The
`-tags full` option enables all standard extension packages (including extra
math functions). For more fine-grained control, see instructions in [cmd/goal
directory](cmd/goal).

# Examples

Aside from the examples found in the documentation, there are various places
with code written in Goal:

* The [examples directory](examples/) contains AoC solutions and a few other short
  scripts.
* The [lib directory](lib/) contains various library utilities. You might want
  to add it to the `GOALLIB` environment variable to simplify import paths.
* The [testdata/scripts directory](testdata/scripts) contains various example
  scripts used in regression testing; they come along an expected result after
  a `/RESULT:` comment.
* The [scripts directory](scripts/) contains a few code generation scripts.

Here's how a Goal script looks like:

```
/ Handle command-line arguments: script name + optional file.
(2<#ARGS)and:error"USAGE: goal wordstats.goal [file]"
/ Read STDIN or filename given by last argument; lowercase everything.
src:_ 'read?[1=#ARGS;STDIN;*|ARGS]
/ Get all words (Unicode letters + dashes).
words:rx/[\p{L}-]+/[src;-1]
/ Print number of words; number of distinct words; five most frequent words.
say(#words;#dw:?words;5@!>dw!=%words)
```

See the tutorial for detailed explanations on a similar example with syntax
highlighting!

# Tooling

* [ari](https://github.com/semperos/ari): interactive programming environment
  built on top of Goal with a dedicated SQL mode (by @semperos).
* [goal2html](cmd/goal2html): html markup generation for Goal source.
* [gw](https://github.com/bleedsa/gw): derived interpreter with sqlite support (by @bleedsa).
* [jupyter kernel](https://github.com/semperos/goal_jupyter_kernel) for Goal
  (by @semperos).
* [vim-goal](https://codeberg.org/anaseto/vim-goal) : vim files for Goal.

# Contribute

User testing and bug reports are welcome! Feel free to open an issue, send a
pull request, or send a patch by email.

See the [implementation notes](docs/implementation.md) to get started about the
internals. You might want to check [problems.md](docs/problems.md) and old
issues before submitting a new issue.

---

# v1.4.0 2025-09-15

Source: https://github.com/wrnrlr/goal-mirror/blob/master/CHANGES.md

# v1.4.0 2025-09-15

* Support weedout `r^S` and replicate `r#S` forms with regexp left, without
  requiring explicit conversion into a function with `{r x}` or `r[]`. Feature
  suggested by oantolin on the matrix chat.
* Make buffered writer filehandles and pipes automatically flush their buffers
  on non-panic exit (see issue #56).
* Fix bug in `"c"$I` when I is internally a byte-slice but doesn't correspond
  to ASCII text (see issue #53).
* Fix edge case of integer application with a single gap argument `i[]` (see
  issue #55). It now returns a monadic projection instead of nonsensical
  output mixing an internal gap value and fill error values.
* Go API: new `FlushWriters` exported function in `os` package that calls flush
  on any open buffered writer filehandles or pipes.

# v1.3.0 2025-06-22

* Support `S run` and `..[s:S;...]run` forms where `S` is a list of strings
  corresponding to a list of lines. Any missing newline is appended, including
  for the last line. Similar to using `(("\n"/-S)+"\n")run`. Feature suggested
  by effbiae on the matrix chat.
* New `lib/flag.goal` library of user-defined functions for command-line flag
  parsing.
* New extension package `encoding/base64` providing base64 encoding
  functionality.
* New convenience `-tags full` build option that enables all standard extension
  packages (currently `archive/zip`, `encoding/base64`, `math`, `os`).
* Fix case of unhelpful right-value shape handling in deep amend of dictionary
  when the first depth is indexed by a single atom key. If the right-value
  wasn't an atom, you would redundantly need to enlist it, which was
  inconvenient and was inconsistent with how deep amend of an array is handled.
  Now things like `dict..key[0 1]+:2 3` work as expected (instead of throwing a
  length mismatch error).
* Fix panic case when using dict syntax incorrectly (see issue #52).
* Use fast-path for `='` when the left argument is not a function nor a generic
  array. This makes use of `=` in generic code avoid performance regressions,
  like we did for other arithmetic and comparison primitives in the previous
  release.
* Optimize away some simple cases of dead local assignments in lambdas. In
  particular, for a local variable `a`, using `a[i]:b` instead of `@[a;i;:;b]`
  now generates the exact same code if `a` is known to not be used afterwards.

# v1.2.0 2025-03-23

This release focuses on auditing the code, searching for any bugs in
edge-cases, while refactoring and commenting the codebase for improving future
maintainability. Most changes are not user-visible but, as a result of the
process, there are still a few fixes and small improvements worth mentioning:

* Properly extend `x»y` and `x«y` for `x` longer than `y` following [BQN's
  semantics](https://mlochbaum.github.io/BQN/doc/shift.html). Previously Goal
  did not follow completely well-defined semantics in that edge-case. Even if
  unlikely to lead to mistakes, there's still a subtle thing to keep in mind
  when `x` is longer than `y` and both have different types: if `x` is of type
  `"I"` and `y` is of type `"N"` then `x«y` will be of type `"I"`, without
  promoting `x` values to `"N"` (as would have happened if `x` were shorter).
* Extend shifts on dict pairs by shifting both keys and values.
* Fix return type in edge-case `n«I` when `n` was an integer floating-point
  number. It's now properly `"N"` but previously was `"I"` by mistake. It was
  unlikely to lead to buggy code in practice (due to implicit conversions) but
  was still incorrect.
* Make scan `f\[x;y;…]` consistently return an empty list of type compatible
  with type of seed `x` when there are no iterations because `y` (or any extra
  argument) is empty. Also, when all the arguments are atoms, scan would
  inconsistently return either `f[x;y]` or `,f[x;y;…]`: the result is now
  enlisted in all cases, as expected.
* Better optimize classify `%X` and `ocount` by using a single-pass algorithm
  that optimistically starts storing results as bytes and, if a result would
  overflow at some point, it upgrades to larger-sized integers before
  continuing.
* Code for “case” with three or more arguments has been improved and should be
  a bit faster.
* The dyadic forms of `+' -' *' %' &' |' <' >'` make use of a fast path using
  the pervasive equivalents without “each”. This can help generic code that
  takes a function argument avoid a potentially surprising performance drop.
* More BCE (Bound Check Elimination) hints in various places.

# v1.1.0 2025-02-17

This release focuses on performance improvements with SIMD on amd64 using the
various SSE extensions up to SSE4.2 (no AVX yet). As we only require SSE
extensions, which are nowadays pretty-much everywhere, they're enabled by
default but can be disabled by using the `-tags nosse4` build option.  The
release also provides various non-SIMD optimizations as well as a few bug fixes
and minor new language features.

Language and library improvements:

* New projection syntactic sugar for passing local variables from parent
  context by naming them in the parameter list before a `|`: `{[a;b|c;d]…}` now
  expands to `{[a;b;c;d]…}[a;b]`.
* Allow empty names in lambda parameter list for unused arguments.
* Allow negative indices in amend, like for normal indexing (see issue #26).
* New `pp` and `pps` pretty-printing functions in `lib/fmt.goal` that handle
  any kind of values with automatic type and suitable precision detection. The
  `pp` function uses the `tput` command to detect the number of lines and
  columns available for display.
* All functions from `lib/fmt.goal` now also handle formatting items of
  arbitrary values, using recursion as needed to format nested floats in
  generic arrays, both for fmt.tbl and fmt.dict. Along the way, fix regression
  (introduced by 0.39.0) in fmt.dict for dicts containing only numeric or
  string atom values.  The formatting functions now also stringify keys if
  necessary.

Optimizations:

* Optimize most atomic arithmetic and boolean operations using SSE, in
  particular for byte-sized integers (including booleans) and floats: over 80
  plain Go functions (with simple loops, like arithmetic ones) are replaced
  with SSE-based assembly functions instead.  Note: behavior for NaNs
  with min/max and `sign` is not the same as the non-optimized build, and sums
  of floats may result in slightly different precision. Use the `-tags nosse4`
  build option to get standard floating-point behavior if necessary (if there
  is demand, we might provide more refined tags to disable only some cases of
  fast floating-point math in ulterior versions).
* Many operations now avoid a redundant memclr, which improves performance of
  fast operations (like most arithmetic) when allocating large arrays.
* Overhead of refcount handling for built-in immutable values has been
  considerably reduced: in particular, higher-order projection-heavy functional
  code is faster than before.
* Add hints in various places for helping BCE (Bound Check Elimination).
* Optimize away various arithmetic special cases like `0+N`, `1*N`, and
  so on.
* Improve special code for `,/A`: we now pre-allocate the total capacity
  avoiding the need for resizes and memclr (when possible).
* Improve performance of `&I` and filter/replicate on boolean inputs with large
  blocks of zeros and ones by vectorized jumping over said blocks.
* Improve performance of “case” `X I'Y` for boolean `I`, in particular for
  arrays `X` and `Y` of bytes. Fixed bug in edge-case in “case” along the way.
* Improve short and medium-range buffer caching for numeric slices of
  variable-size types (used in radix sort and search functions). Adjusted some
  thresholds in search functions over integer arrays (trade memory for
  performance for short and medium-sized arrays).
* Special code for the `,\x` scan form, as well as improved special code for
  `&\I` and `|\I` on booleans.
* Special code for "first where" idiom `*&x`.
* Optimize roll `i?y` for powers of two (previously only done for 2).
* Optimize reverse `|I` for bytes (using SWAR and math/bits.ReverseBytes64).
* When processing many time values at once, make `time` return a compact array
  of bytes for byte-sized entries (like with `"day"`, `"month"`, `"date"`, or
  `"clock"`).
* Merge lambda partial application followed by immediate application
  `{[…]…}[…][…]` into `{[…]…}[…;…]` when possible. Such kind of application
  chain is easily generated for example when using field expression syntax or
  the new named partial application lambda syntax.

Bug fixes and minor specification adjustments and corrections:

* Update/fix return type of `sign N` to `"N"` instead of `"I"` for consistency
  (like for `_N`, `uc N`, and `abs N`). Conversion to integer was unlikely to
  be desirable there anyway, given result is usually used to multiply by some
  other floats, forcing another conversion back to `"N"`; this shouldn't break
  any user code in practice thanks to implicit conversions between integers and
  floats, but it's technically not a 100% compatible fix.
* Remove buggy command `"zone"` of `time` builtin as it was unlikely to be used
  in any meaningful and correct way directly as currently designed: using a
  unix time and layout with time zone abbreviation and offset is the practical
  way instead. With respect to backward compatibility, this change is to be
  interpreted as removing a badly specified edge-case misfeature nobody ever
  used or cared about.
* Fix optimized idioms `*<x` and `*>x` for empty arrays and arrays containing
  NaNs.
* Fix output of `help["in"]` and `help["¿"]` by using a more robust method when
  parsing the help (see issue #25).
* Fix refcount issue in lambda with a single unused argument.
* Go API: The `MarkImmutable` method now returns the immutable value; this
  small signature update is not 100% compatible, but it should not break any
  user code in practice, as there wasn't any return value before. Using the
  returned marked value is often more convenient and optimization-friendly
  (thanks to improved refcount handling for immutable values).

# v1.0.0 2024-10-31

This release is the first stable release.  It introduces read-only file system
values and a few new OS builtins.  It also polishes various secondary parts of
the language and API, with a few last minor breaking changes. The minimum
required Go version is now 1.22.

* New `dirfs` OS builtin returning a read-only file system value rooted at a
  system directory, which can be used as left argument with `import`, `glob`,
  `open`, `read`, and `stat`. Note that as a result `stat` is now a dyad and
  accepts a left argument. Also, the new `subfs` builtin can be used to derive
  a file system rooted at a subtree.
* New `glob` OS builtin returning file names matching glob pattern(s).
* New `abspath` OS builtin returning a cleaned absolute representation of a
  path. As a particular case, it can be used to get the current working
  directory with `abspath"."` (even after `chdir`, unlike `env"PWD"`), or to
  clean an absolute path in a portable way, so it is quite versatile for a
  single builtin. Name is taken from `abspath` which was implemented in ari by
  semperos first. It seems to be the similar to `os.path.abspath` in python.
  It does not resolve symlinks, so it's simpler and faster than `realpath(3)`.
  If given a list of path elements, `abspath` first joins them into a single
  path.
* Rework and clarify `import` rules with GOALLIB: the empty extension case
  behaves now like `(dirfs env"GOALLIB")import s`. In particular, it uses
  slash-separated paths on all platforms, and the GOALLIB environment variable
  can contain at most one directory (the help never mentioned it accepted a
  list of directories anyway). The new file system value imports should allow
  for enough flexibility, while being easier to reason about.
* Handles are now callable, providing both some introspection and some extra
  functionality that may be specific to a kind of handle (like `"sync"` for
  file writer handles) and thus are not worth a new verb.
* `open` and `run` now accept a dict as left argument, allowing to configure
  the command's stdin, stdout, and stderr. Also, `STDERR` is now unbuffered by
  default.
* New `rt.get"os"` form to get the operating system's name, `rt.get"pfx"` form
  to get the current eval prefix for globals, and `rt.get"loc"` form to get the
  current eval location.
* New `rt.get"v"` form that returns a version string informing about goal's
  version and extensions, replacing old meaning for `"v"`. The `rt.get"g"` and
  `rt.get"f"` forms have been removed: they're redundant and easily obtained
  using `.'.rt.get"!"` and filter if needed; they were inspired from `\v` and
  `\f` in ngn/k, but those are not primitives, they're system commands
  available only in REPL.  Instead, add `rt.get"kw"` for getting the list of
  verbal keywords, which was previously only accessible from Go.
* Make `exp` and `log` into dyads accepting the base as left argument. Remove
  obsolete `pow` from `lib/math.goal`.
* New `"r"$` form that either quotes regexp metacharacters from a string or
  retrieves the string pattern from a regexp.
* New `lib/fs.goal` library of user-defined functions providing file listing
  and tree walking functionality for the new file system values (`ls`, `walk`).
* New `lib/os.goal` library of user-defined functions providing some extra
  os-related functionality (`volume`, `mkdirp`, `rmtree`).
* Remove support in `open` for synonymous shell/Perl-like modes: it didn't make
  much sense to have both, so remove the redundant ones before stable release.
* Now `$x` gives `!""` for empty lists of strings and `?0` for empty lists of
  floats, making all empty lists of specific types have default string
  representations corresponding to simple and short monadic applications. As an
  added benefit, those are recognized and optimized by Goal's current basic
  constant-folding pass. The `"v"$` parsing form has been updated to recognize
  instead the new forms, so that it remains a proper partial inverse of `$x`.
* Update `json` encoding and decoding to preserve source key order of JSON
  objects. In case sorting is desired, for example to verify with match if two
  decoded objects contain the same key/value pairs, irrespectively of key
  order, it has now to be done manually: see the new `lib/dict.goal` for a
  solution.
* Update number generator using the new `math/rand/v2` package: we break
  repeatability from (testing) fixed seeds so that we won't need to support
  both `math/rand` and `math/rand/v2` in the future. Repeatability when setting
  the seed should be backward-compatible from now on.
* Implement tail call optimization for tail calls with special variable `o`. 
* Tetradic amend performance improvements with arithmetic operations and when
  using mixed numeric types.
* Improve csv performance for typical inputs by using a custom parser and
  writer, inspired from encoding/csv, but specialized to Goal's case: the whole
  input is available in memory, so in particular unquoted inputs and quoted
  inputs that don't use quote escapes or newlines don't need a new
  heap-allocated copy. Also, for simplicity, we disallow non-ASCII characters
  for the field separator, as it's unlikely to be useful very often.
* Make multi-line block comments starting with `/` and ending with single `\`
  ignore trailing spaces. Previous behavior was inspired from ngn/k, and while
  syntax highlighting could make up for this, it wasn't intuitive that trailing
  whitespace could change comment parsing.
* Fix issue in REPL scanning of comments when they contain delimiters (see
  issue #18).
* Fix potential parsing panic issue when parsing code using incorrect syntax.
* Fix incorrect parsing edge-case around `..` followed by negative number
  literal without spacing.
* Fix case of extra empty records in csv parsing (see issue #19).
* Fix potential liveness analysis bug with early returns.
* Fix branching-related bug in constant folding.
* Fix various inconsistent uses of location when formatting time values. Now
  location always defaults to UTC. Also, document in the FAQ that location is
  used either for formatting (integer time value) or parsing (other kinds of
  time values), but not both, defaulting to UTC for the other (see issue #22).
* Fix lambda signature issue in handling of special prefixes `p.` and `q.` with
  special names `y` and `z` in compositions and field expressions.
* Go API: new `io/fs` package providing read-only file system and file
  abstraction for Goal based on the standard `fs` package. File systems created
  using this new package are supported out-of-the-box by the builtins of the
  `os` package, like for `dirfs`.
* Go API: export `NewOSError` in the `os` package to help extensions use the
  same conventions for describing operating-system errors.
* Go API: export `NewDirFS` in the `os` package so that extensions can define
  `dirfs path` file system values from Go.
* Go API: New `help` package that exports a function with built-in REPL help,
  for use with the `cmd` package.
* Go API: Rename awkwardly named `cmd.Cmd` into `cmd.Run`.
* Go API: Move the `LessT` method of `BV` interface into a separate `OrderedBV`
  interface, so that unordered values don't need to implement it (defaulting to
  lexicographic type comparison). This change is unlikely to break any code, as
  interfaces are implemented implicitly, and it should simplify definition of
  new kinds of unordered values.
* Go API: New `RegisterExtension` and `Version` methods on Context.
* Go API: Allow `Eval` within variadic functions too, like with `EvalPackage`.
* Go API: New `archive/zip` and `math` packages, as optional extensions.
* Go API: Add a convenience `GetS` method for dicts `*D` in `goal` package,
  similar to `Get`, but for the typical case where the key is a string.
* Go API: Export `Rand` field of `Context` using new `math/rand/v2` package.
* Go API: make `V.Apply` into a variadic function and remove redundant
  `V.Apply2` (minor breaking change). This should make typical `Apply` uses
  with more than one argument easier to write. Note that we keep `V.ApplyAt` as
  a faster specialized version for the one argument case, like with `@` vs `.`.
  Also, note that `Apply` from `Callable` as well as `VariadicFunc` don't take
  a variadic parameter, because they're meant to be implemented, but rarely
  used directly.

# v0.44.0 2024-09-12

* Add `s%s` “glob match” form: it's more convenient than regexps for typical
  path match patterns. The path separator is always `/` independently from the
  platform as in Go's `path.Match`, not `filepath.Match`, so that it can
  portably be used for URLs and other kinds of slash-based paths.
* When sorting floating point values, NaNs are now ordered before other values.
  Previously, sorting data with NaNs was not supported.  Moreover, all
  self-search and search primitives have been extended to support NaN values
  too, following new match semantics where `0n~0n` holds (minor breaking
  change).  The rationale is that sort, match `~`, and search primitives, are
  not arithmetic operations limited to numbers and strings, but more high-level
  operations working on arbitrary values.  Moreover, reflexivity is quite
  desirable for match `~`.  Note that plain arithmetic atomic comparisons still
  return 0 when either operand is NaN, following the usual floating point
  conventions from the IEEE 754 standard.
* Accept `@[x;i;f]` (and `@[x;i;f;z]`) form where `f` is an array (usually of
  functions) instead of a single function, with semantics similar to
  `@[;;]/[X;i;f]`, but recursively handling nested inputs. The main motivation
  is to allow amending values at different indices/keys using different
  functions.  Also, note that amend will try to apply (non-array) value `f`
  whether it's a function or not, so `f` can actually contain any kind of
  callable value, not only a function.
* Support `p.o` in field expressions as a reference to the self-recursive `o`
  of the parent function (it could previously only refer to an explicitly
  defined `o` variable in the parent context).
* Support amend sugar for field assignments in dict-amend as in
  `d..[a[&b<0]+:1]`, expanding to `d..[a:@[a;&b<0;+;1]]`.
* Support multiple `p.` prefixes in nested field-expressions.
* Add `rt.try` builtin, similar to `.[f;y;f]`, but it passes an error value
  dict with the whole error stack trace as message. It is intended for cases
  were performance is not important, but extra location information is needed.
* Add `lib/path.goal` library of user-defined functions for manipulating
  `/`-separated paths.
* Add `lib/table.goal` library of user-defined functions related to table
  manipulation.
* Add `examples/lil.goal` with translations of examples from Lil's manual.
* Fix idiom recognition in edge-case where a non-flat chained application parse
  tree could result in idioms not being optimized.
* Fix issue in `.s`, `rt.get["v"]` and `rt.get["g"]` when a global variable is
  statically present in the code but not assigned yet. In such cases, a gap
  value was produced, instead of a panic.
* Fix out of bounds index check regression in deep amend code.

# v0.43.0 2024-08-11

* Make zero value fill for `()` be `0#""` instead of `()`. The rationale is
  that `()` is unlikely to be more useful in any context and has the
  inconvenient that `()~*()`, which is usually a math property that only atoms
  satisfy. The reason `0#""` was chosen over `!0` is that an empty generic list
  can happen quite naturally in things like `csv 'read"file.csv"` if the file
  is empty, when you usually expect a generic list of lists of strings.
  However, `!0` could maybe have made sense too: the choice is somewhat
  arbitrary (like `()` was to begin with). Returning an error or panic could
  have been a possibility too, but we usually try to avoid those in pure
  operations if chosing a default can help make a typical edge-case work, and
  `0#""` is a kind of empty list like `()`, so it's much less likely of
  breaking any existing code. Also, for reference, ngn/k returns `""` for
  `*()`, but in Goal lists of strings are already a specialized type with `""`
  as zero value, so that case is already covered.
* Make empty regular expression `rx//` and `:` (fills for generic lists
  containing functions) into false values, like other kinds of fill values.
  Also, use `error"fill"` as fill for non-empty generic lists whose first
  element isn't one of the core types, as relying on a fill value in such cases
  wouldn't work anyway, unless we add some kind of Go interface to provide a
  way to define custom fill values (which we could in the future).
* Allow `0` as base in encode `I\`, for convenience. Using a zero is equivalent
  to using an integer larger than the maximum value being encoded, so it can be
  used as a default leftmost base.
* Make `"v"$`, `json` and `time` return error dicts with extra machine-readable
  information (the error message as reported by `e..msg` like when used in
  interpolation or `print` is still the same). Make similar improvements in
  `os` package.
* Simplify `lib/mods.goal` and keep only adverbial forms involving non-ASCII
  each-right, as the others were only didactical in purpose. Also, add
  `reshape` in `lib/k.goal`.
* Simplify and make more regular edge-case of comment parsing: now after `;`,
  `(`, `{` and `[`, a space is not needed to start a comment unless there's no
  expression on the right, following the same rules as other non-adverbial uses
  of `'`, `\`, and `` ` ``. The case of comments is still a bit different from
  the others, because they span until the end of the line, not of the
  expression, but that's as close as it can get to the others.
* Fix scanning of quoting constructs using `` ` `` as delimiter in REPL (by
  semperos).
* Fix edge-case in scanning of `..` when followed by number.
* Now all panics with "too many arguments" error messages always show the
  number of received arguments between parens (can be useful if arguments were
  passed using `.` and number of arguments is not syntactically evident).

# v0.42.0 2024-07-14

* If a script returns an error value dict with a key `code`, the corresponding
  value is used to set the exit error code, following the same convention as
  the `run` builtin. Only portable integer values within `[1,125]` are
  supported, the default being `1`.
* Implement discard/ignore `` `expr `` syntax using non-adverbial backquote
  (suggested by @semperos, feature inspired by `#_` in Clojure).
* Add `rt.get"!"` to get only global names (without values), in a similar way
  as `GlobalNames` from Go API does. Also, document `rt.get["@";x]` (to be used
  only for debug purposes).
* Fix potential stack-handling bug when returning early from within an
  incomplete operation.
* Using `eval` on code that ends in an empty expression returned a gap value,
  despite the fact that such value is normally not possible to write in Goal.
  It returns `1` (for success) in such cases now.  Note that `Context.Eval` of
  the Go API still returns a gap value, because gap as default makes sense
  there and is useful to avoid echo in REPL when expression ends in `;`, for
  example.
* Fix bug in local vs global resolution in single colon (usually local) single
  and multi assignment for variables that have a dot (catched by fuzzing).
* Fix a few remaining issues in desugared code pretty-printing.
* Allow empty list of non-integer type in replicate `f#y` and weedout `f^y` for
  `f[y]`, as this can help avoid some typical edge-cases. This was actually a
  regression and could make panic one example from the tutorial when input file
  was empty.
* Go API: export new `ExitError` type in `cmd` package, providing a way to
  inspect the exit code associated with a returned error value (defaulting to
  `1`).
* Go API: explicitly document `NewGap` various usages (non-fixed projection
  argument, default value for undefined globals, and absence of returned value
  in `Run` or `Eval`), and that, like `Panic` values, gap values are not meant
  to be used explicitly from Goal code.
* Go API: rename `VariadicFun` using the more usual convention `VariadicFunc`
  for function types in Go (minor breaking change).

# v0.41.0 2024-07-06

* Error values are now callable and support a method-like `e..msg` call that
  can be used to produce a string error message from any kind of error. If `.e`
  is a string, number or array, a default string representation is returned,
  but otherwise it applies `(.e)..msg`, which is further applied on `.e` if it
  is a function, and the final result is formatted into a default string
  representation.  The idea behind this feature is that `$e` on an error does
  not produce an error message that is ready for user consumption, so `e..msg`
  works a bit like `e.Error()` in Go, and is interpolable. Also, for
  convenience, the `e..msg` call is implicit in string interpolation like
  `"$e"`, as well as `print e` and `say e`, because those contexts usually
  expect an error message, not a program representation of it.  The name `msg`
  was chosen because it's short and is already used by some error dicts
  returned in the `os` package.
* Expand `..a[2]` as `{x["a";2]}` and similarly `..a..b[3]` as
  `{x["a";"b";3]}`, instead of successive monadic applications `{x["a"][2]}`,
  to make it consistent with how an explicit `x..a[2]` already expands as
  `x["a";2]`.  Both expansions behave the same when `x` is a dictionary/table,
  which is the most common case, but the “application merging” expansion is
  closer to how you would write it by hand without sugar, and it also is more
  convenient when implementing custom values in extensions. For example, an
  hypothetical `heap` extension could easily provide a method-like looking API
  where you would write `x..push[v]` and `x..pop[v]` (where `x` is a `heap`
  value) just by implementing the `Callable` interface for the new value type.
* Allow dict `f[y]` in “cut where” `f_Y`, using the values for cutting. Rarely
  useful, but consistent with filter/weedout.
* Fix bug when restoring execution state after eval: global multi-assignment
  information (within a lambda within eval) could be lost.
* A few improvements in debug info with `-d`. Fix a couple of issues in
  desugared code pretty-printing.
* Refactor code that maps opcodes to source positions, setting more
  sensible/accurate positions in some edge cases.
* Go API: add `Prefix` option in `scan/html` package to prepend a custom prefix
  to HTML class names for styling. Add `--prefix` option with same meaning in
  the `cmd/goal2html` tool.
* Go API: export regexp boxed value type as struct type `*R`. Use `NewR` to
  create a regexp value, and the `Regexp` method to retrieve the underlying
  `regexp.Regexp` object.
* Go API: add explicit `NewGap` function that simply returns a zero value for
  `V`, for clarity and documentation purposes.
* Go API: export boxed error value type as struct type `*Error`, and make the
  `Error` method return that type instead of `V` (minor breaking-change).
* Go API: add `NewDict` function, similar to `NewD` but taking `Array` values
  as input instead of `V`, to make dict creation more convenient in some cases.

# v0.40.0 2024-06-19

This is mostly a polishing release, except for the new `scan/html` package that
allows us to efficiently embed the syntax highlighter in the documentation
generator. The FAQ also got an entry discussing future stability and
compatibility expectations after the upcoming v1.0.0 release, maybe at some
point later this year.

* Allow debug flag `-d` with `-e` option too.
* Allow atomic `y` in `f#y` and `f^y` when `1~#f[y]`.
* Allow case `N'[X;Y]` if `N` contains only integers.
* Allow dict values to be used directly in multi-assignment.
* Return sorted keys in `read` for directory (like for `stat`).
* Fix issue that could sometimes result in incorrect rank computation (as used
  by adverbs) for functions obtained from partial application of a function of
  rank > 2 when gaps were not all explicit.
* Various small refactorings. Improvements in test coverage for `os` package.
* Go API: new `scan/html` package for html highlighting of Goal code from Go
  too. This allows to embed syntax highlighting within a markup language
  tool like frundis, avoiding the need for external calls.
* Go API: `cmd` package now sets `Config.ProgramName` to `os.Args[0]` by
  default.

# v0.39.0 2024-06-08

* Support field variable string interpolation in field expressions: things like
  `d.."$a"` now properly expand `d..a` within the string. We also allow
  explicit `"$d..a"` and `"${d..a}"` in string interpolation now. The new
  accepted syntax is useful when using dict values to produce a string
  template.
* Implement experimental fold while form `F/[f;x;y;...]`, identical to a fold
  but checking `f x` on the accumulator for early exit on each iteration. It
  also accepts a maximal number of iterations instead of a condition function
  `f`.  Following the same idea, implement scan while form `F\[f;x;y;...]` too.
  Fold while is particularly useful in scripting when returning early due to an
  error (see example in examples/goalx).
* Remove `rt.ofs` (breaking-change), as it's quite unidiomatic in Goal and
  error-prone: I never used it (always using join `s/` instead), and it was
  only there due to AWK/Perl influence. In the rare case were concatenating a
  long list of large strings before `print` could be problematic from a
  memory-usage point of view, it's possible to divide such a list in smaller
  parts and process them separately.
* Add short man page with command-line usage details.
* Optimize implementation of “fields” `s!s` when left argument is ASCII.
* Add basic constant folding pass in compiler for a few idiomatic forms:
  `,cst`, `!cst`, `cst dyad`. The idea is to avoid unwanted small allocations
  in idiomatic code. Note that `!i` is only computed at compile-time for very
  small constant `i`.
* The debug form `rt.get["vinfo";x]` for retrieving type (and other internal)
  information about a value has been renamed into `rt.get["@";x]`. A reminder
  that such form should only be used for debug purposes (changes in the
  implementation internals may change the results).
* Go API: add a convenience `Import` function in `os` package for importing all
  variadics at once with an optional prefix.
* Go API: add a convenience `Get` method for dicts `*D` in `goal` package.

# v0.38.0 2024-05-25

* Make `0i` integer value falsy (in `?`, `and` and `or`), so that `|/!0` is
  falsy. This should avoid a typical pitfall, and be backwards compatible
  enough, as previous code depending on `0i` being true is unlikely (given
  small user base). Make `0n` and `-0w` falsy too, for consistency, though it's
  unlikely to be useful (except in json encoding, see below). Add support for
  new false values in monadic `~`.
* Allow extra optional string argument in regexp application to specify the
  kind of wanted result, disabling default "smart" behavior: `"i"` for an integer
  0 or 1 result (only in dyadic usage without specified number of matches),
  `"s"` for getting the whole text match (whether or not the regexp has groups,
  both with or without specified number of matches). The default behavior is
  nice most of the time, but disabling submatch results can be useful to use a
  regexp with grouping parens for both usages, instead of having to write a
  different regexp. It can be useful too if the regexp comes from an untrusted
  source.
* Make `json` encode `-0w` as `false` and `0w` as `true`, so that it's possible
  to encode `false` and `true`, and make `0n` encode as `null`. Parsing has
  been updated to also use the new boolean and null values, for consistency and
  simplicity (BREAKING CHANGE, you can apply `~~` to convert to integer
  booleans as before, because `-0w` is now a false value). This means that the
  user has to be careful to not encode infinity values by mistake, but the
  alternatives weren't perfect either.  Also, fixed issue with `()` being
  encoded as `null` instead of `[]`.
* Go API: add GlobalNames and Keywords methods for Context to help with things
  like auto-completion.

# v0.37.0 2024-05-10

* Improve row filtering in `X#t`: now row filters are applied immediately
  before processing the next row filter, instead of computing all of them on
  the whole table before applying them together.  This change should make some
  typical queries faster by making successive filters only apply to the subset
  of rows kept by previous filters. The new behavior is compatible with the old
  one except in the unlikely suspicious case where a secondary filter would
  assume no rows were filtered out by the previous one.
* Be more strict with comment parsing: things like `(/2)` now parse as `(/)2`,
  that is `2/`, instead of as a comment. Before, only specific cases like
  `(/)`, with a closing delimiter, used the adverbial meaning. Will probably
  not break any existing programs in practice. Also, `\ / comment` is now
  properly parsed as `(\)` instead of throwing a "non-adverbial form" parse
  error.
* Do not redefine `h` nor `help` in REPL mode when they've already been defined
  as globals (in `-e cmd` or `script` before going into REPL with `-i`).
* Fix off-by-one bug in classify `%X` optimized code-path for sorted `X`: if
  there were 3 classes the result wrongly got marked as boolean as if there
  were less than 2.
* Go API: export ApplyFloatFunc and Apply2FloatFunc making it possible to
  extend Goal with more math functions easily.

# v0.36.0 2024-03-28

* Allow partial substr for strings: `s[;]`. When ommitted, first argument
  defaults to 0 and second defaults to string length, so that behavior is
  similar than for arrays, i.e for example `s[]` is just `s`.
* Add `rt.get["vinfo";y]` form to inspect value `y` internals (should only used
  for debug or learning purposes).
* Implement `"b"$d` and `"c"$d` for dict inputs, keeping keys as long as length
  is preserved.
* Optimize div `(-i)!I` for power of two divisor (mod `i!I` already optimized
  that case).
* The `i!s` padding form now uses length in code points instead of number of
  bytes. Ideally, we would use a more accurate measure of width, like the one
  provided by the go-runewidth package, but we want to avoid dependencies for
  now (we could copy it under `vendor/` if there is demand for it).
* Add `examples/tables.goal` with examples from new “work with tables”
  documentation chapter.
* Fix panic case in overflowing small-range integer optimization check.
* Fix error message prefix for dicts in dyadic arithmetic.
* Implementation: simplify and improve encode `I\` code.

# v0.35.0 2024-02-26

* Optimization: arithmetic operations only checked reusability for the first
  argument matching the result type, so sometimes code would fall back to
  allocating a new result even if the other argument was reusable. Now both are
  checked for reusability.
* Improve `i#y` and `!I` performance by copying cycles in blocks.
* Refine matching rules for `~` between empty arrays: now empty numeric arrays
  still match between them even if of different type (int vs float), but empty
  string arrays and empty generic arrays don't. The previous rule was a bit too
  permissive without being useful. The rule for floats vs ints follows from the
  fact that things like `0.0 1.0` and `0 1` match for conveniency, even though
  they're of different type, because they can be used with same semantics
  anywhere (except in overflowing operations).
* Fix a case of bad empty list type in group by with sorted indices.
* Fix stack handling bug in `@[f;y;f]` and `.[f;y;f]` on panic.
* Parse empty arrays of specifc types in `"v"$`, which kind of got forgotten.
* Go API: add pfx argument in Compile method, with similar semantics as in
  EvalPackage.
* Add `examples/dplyr.goal` goal translations of examples from
  <https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/dplyr.html>.

# v0.34.0 2024-02-19

* Switch minimum Go version from 1.18 to 1.20 for building Goal (actually this
  was already the case for v0.33.0, but it wasn't documented).
* Optimize `"b"$` conversion between arrays of bytes and strings, avoiding the
  need for a copy by marking arrays of bytes as not reusable.
* Remove experimental span `i$i`: it was just a very minor conveniency form
  that wasn't very useful due to being restricted to integer atoms (unlike the
  more useful arithmetic primitive with same name from BQN that inspired it).
* Extend `s/` by making it right string-list atomic, so that it's a proper
  inverse of split `s\` which was already a (string) atomic function.
* Implement `o` as recursive self-reference in lambdas, like in ngn/k.
* Refine type information in many error messages.
* Implementation: various refactorings making the code easier to get into.

# v0.33.0 2024-02-14

* Allow non-identifier keys in dict syntax, for example `..[2:e1;"b c":e2]`.
* Expand assignment in field expressions to more cases: all non-field and
  non-projection (not `p.` prefixed) variables can now be assigned. Also, the
  experimental `g.` prefix has now become `q.` (meaning “quote”, though not
  really in a lisp-like sense) and is now used to insert as-is (without
  projecting) both local and global variables with same resolution rules as in
  regular lambdas.
* Improve performance of `time` builtin on long arrays of dates with a more
  vectorized implementation. Also, the `"date"`, `"clock"`, `"weekday"` and
  `"zone"` time commands now return a flipped version when given a list of
  dates: it's both more performant and convenient; previous behavior was an
  oversight (minor-breaking change).
* The `time` builtin now accepts `"date"` as format argument (not only as
  command), so that you can pass a date in `(year;month;day;...)` form.
* Allow `(f;...)#t` with `f` function too, not only `I` and `S`. Also, use `t`
  in the help to represent dicts with string keys and columnar values.
* Remove the experimental `¨` adverb: I played around with it and decided it
  wasn't worth it.
* Add special code for `S[I;i]` and `S[I;i;i]` fast indexings.
* `$'I` now formats `0i` as `"0i"`.
* Fix funny args parsing: `{[x]-1+x}5` now returns `4`, not `-6`.

# v0.32.0 2024-02-03

* The `csv` builtin has been reworked to return a list of columns instead of a
  list of rows (breaking-change). This was an oversight, but a list of columns
  is almost always what you want and you would use flip `+` every time.
  Performance is also better than returning rows and then doing a flip
  afterwards (though it could still be improved for large files by processing
  in smaller blocks).
* Expressions `.. expr` now support implicit arguments `x`, `y` and `z`, like
  lambdas. If a field is named `y`, one has to access it explicitly with
  `x..y`. This change makes it possible to access the whole table as `x`, but
  can also make expressions work as lambdas that implicitly pass surrounding
  variables as extra arguments (like compositions but more flexible). Also, in
  addition to the projection prefix `p.`, there's now a global `g.` prefix
  that can be used to insert a global variable without projecting; it can be
  used in compositions too: `g.a-+` becomes `{a-x+y}` instead of projecting
  onto `a`.
* Simple local assignment and assignment operations (not amending ones) in `..
  expr` for `x`, `y` and `z` is supported, but not yet for fields nor globals.
* For dict with string keys, handle `d[;S]` and `d[I;]` with omitted args with
  table-like indexing instead of dict-like.
* Fix bug in deep amend in which z wasn't properly indexed.

# v0.31.0 2024-01-29

This release expands dict functionality to make it easier to work with dicts
with string keys, including some table-like functionality.

* Add special syntax to evaluate expressions under dicts using fields as
  variables.  There are `.. expr` and `value .. expr` forms;  `.. expr` is
  actually just sugar for a lambda projection (similarly to compositions),
  taking always one non-fixed argument `x`.  Within `expr` variable names like
  `var` (without dot prefix) resolve to `x["var"]`, while other variables are
  passed as extra arguments. The special `p.` prefix can be used to force
  projection onto that variable. If `value` is given, it's passed as argument
  to the `.. expr` lambda projection, and so `d.. expr` is a simple way to
  evaluate an expression under a dict.  Assignment of fields in `expr` is not
  supported, but amend under dict (see below) can be used instead.  Only one
  space (either right or left) around `..` is needed to avoid `value..expr`
  being parsed as a single token meaning `value["expr"]`.
* New `..[a:e1;b:e2]` syntax for defining dicts with string keys, expanding to
  `"a""b"!(e1;e2)`. Also, new `d..[a:e1;b:e2]` amend fields (amend under dict)
  syntax, equivalent to `@[d;"a""b";:;d..(e1;e2)]`.
* When dicts whose values are flat arrays of strings are indexed by integers
  first, we use table-like indexing with optional key-indexing last. This
  allows to use table indexing for string-keyed dicts without having a
  dedicated table type. Also, `X#d` was given specific meaning in the case `d`
  has string keys and `X` is a generic list `(x0;x1[;x2])`: in such case, the
  first element `x0` is used to filter the key/value arrays (either a function
  returning booleans or the booleans directly), and then all the other
  arguments are used to filter the columns, as a conjunction of where clauses
  (and can also be either functions or booleans). The `X^d` form was extended
  similarly.
* Implement deep amend for dicts, and make `d..a[i]` expand to `d["a";i]`
  instead of `d["a"][i]`, so that it's possible to easily amend columns in a
  table-like dict. It can also be useful in extensions to implement values with
  method-like behavior.
* Add `-i` option to interpreter to enter interactive mode after running a
  command string or a script.
* Regexps now accept dictionary inputs.
* Make `d F' d` for two dicts take into account mismatches in keys (for example
  key order), like for primitive arithmetic operators.
* Add a few more utility goal lib functions in `lib/`.
* Optimize some cases of duplicated arguments in composition transformation
  into lambda projection.
* Fix global capture issue in compositions ending in a derived verb.
* Go API: make Help field in Cmd into a function.
* Go API: export MonadicFloatFunc to make it easy for extensions to register
  extra monadic floating point math functions from Go's math package (like
  Gamma, hyperbolic functions, and some Bessel functions), like for example
  with `ctx.RegisterMonad("gamma", goal.MonadicFloatFunc("gamma",
  math.Gamma))`.

# v0.30.0 2024-01-09

* Extend arithmetic operators `+-*%&|` and `,` to more than 2 arguments,
  with meaning equivalent to a fold over the list of arguments, similar to how
  Lisp-like languages extend arithmetic operators.
* Make partial applications of folds and scans (with less arguments than
  expected for the function's rank) return projections even though they're not
  created using projection syntax. We don't do the same for each, as it's less
  typical to fix an argument there, and behavior is independent from the rank
  from the modified function (unlike in scans and folds); things like `#'x`
  already force monadic rank for `#` (without requiring to write `#:`), so for
  consistency we do the same for all kinds of functions and ranks. Note that
  projections using explicit projection syntax, like in `x f'` or `f'[x;]`,
  still work the same as always.
* Report more Unicode-aware column in error messages.
* Refine variable liveness analysis optimization for cond when it's the last
  expression in a lambda.
* Go API: add NewProjection function, IsProjection and IsGap methods so that
  it's possible to create custom projections in extensions.

# v0.29.0 2024-01-03

* Implement decode `I/` generic case using Horner's method so that it accepts
  any inputs as produced by encode `I\`. As a result, it now works for
  non-integer polynomial evaluation too. Now `I\` has been extended too to
  nested arrays such that it's an inverse of decode (for positive integer
  inputs).
* Make `"v"$` parse properly hexadecimal numbers too.
* Allow substr indexing at depth for strings in arrays.
* `s?` now returns `&s` instead of `-1` for out of bounds, so that it's
  consistent with find on arrays (minor breaking change).
* The `nan` verb now also handles `0i` and integer arrays, not only arrays of
  floats and `0n`.
* Implement `i?d` by selecting randomly matching keys and values, returning a
  dict.
* Add missing panic check in `f/x`.

# v0.28.0 2023-12-15

* Repurpose backquote as each-left (BREAKING-CHANGE). Goal already supports several
  quoting constructs, so it was kind of redundant and having each-left like in
  K often comes handy, even though not strictly necessary. Each backquoted
  string can be replaced with a `rq/.../` construct (backquote is also now
  allowed as delimiter).
* Add each-right adverb as `´` and argument dup/swap adverb `¨` (EXPERIMENTAL
  FEATURE) companions to backquote.  The implementation does not currently
  allow adverb keywords, so we don't provide an ASCII alternative, but they are
  merely convenience adverbs anyways: they can be implemented with projections
  and lambdas (see `lib/mods.goal` for common adverbial combinations), and an
  adverbial keyword would not produce much benefit over that.  The rationale
  for the current symbols choice is that they're available in all fonts, are
  used in many natural languages and should hence be accessible on most systems
  without difficult configuration (I hope). Also, `´` is a natural companion to
  backquote even though it's not ASCII.
* Implementation of tacit-compositions by compiling them into lambdas or lambda
  projections, so that we get precise locations for any errors and access to
  tools such as debug `\x`. We also provide the colon suffix for making verbs
  monadic, like if `+:`. Adverbs can also take a colon suffix for monadic case,
  and are dyadic otherwise; this is a minor deviation from K where adding a
  colon to an adverb just creates digraph adverb of unrelated meaning.
* Amend operations now don't require a double colon when global
  (minor breaking-change). The requirement did not make much sense and I think
  the new behavior is the one of other K dialects.
* Put parse value into `"v"$y` so that `.s` is now old `::s` which has been
  made like the monadic version of `:` so that it can be then used in tacit
  compositions at the end (minor breaking change).
* GO API: rename `scan.DyadAssign` into `scan.DyadColon` as it can now also be
  used to refer to the monadic version of an operator.

# v0.27.1 2023-12-03

* Fix remaining immutability issue with `~` due to typos in special code.

# v0.27.0 2023-12-03

* When using `import` (or triadic eval) on the same file (or same string and
  location) with different prefixes, the file is now evaluated once again but
  with the new prefix.  Previously all imports would have to use the same
  prefix. That said, it is recommended to use the same prefix everywhere when
  importing the same file.
* Use multi-line output when using `\x`, instead of compact output.
* Fix missing immutability mark in not `~A` for generic arrays.
* Fix crash with `i#x` for atomic `x` and negative `i`.
* Fix error location entry when an error occurs during execution of lambda
  imported from another file.

# v0.26.0 2023-11-29

* New `var..field` syntactic sugar for `var["field"]` with `..` syntax that
  binds tightly (it's not an operator, just sugar). It's mainly intended to
  make dicts nicer to use. It could also be used by callable user-defined types
  in extensions. Lua uses similar syntactic sugar for tables.
* The `.s` form has been reworked as a partial inverse of `$x` for values whose
  atoms are of numeric, string or regexp types. It does not allow arbitrary
  execution anymore and can now be used for fast enough decoding after
  serialization with `$x`, since it now uses a specialized parser that avoids
  compilation. Think of it as a json alternative that preserves Goal's types
  better for cases when interoperability with non-Goal programs is not
  important. The previous “restricted eval” semantics had even worse
  performance than full-fledged `eval` (due to creation of new evaluation
  context), so it wasn't very useful as a “pure” evaluation primitive.
* Now `$x` always produces a compact string representation of `x`. When
  printing to standard output (via `say x` or `print x`) or standard error
  (`\x`), the usual more human-readable form that may span several lines for
  generic arrays and dicts is produced.
* Now `$x` formats regexps using `rx/PATTERN/` syntax.
* Make `A'` work for generic arrays as an each-kind of deep indexing. In the
  dyadic case, it's equivalent to `{A[x;y]}'`.
* Fix escaping of `$` chararcter within double-quoted strings returned by `$x`,
  so that it's equivalent to a program representation of the string.
* Fix error location information being partially lost when using `import`.  Now
  error location information is correctly propagated.
* Go API: Rework panic handling; rename PanicError into Panic, and make it
  implement the BV interface.  Also, make it into a proper error supporting
  Unwrap.
* Go API: Append method now takes an additional boolean argument that
  determines whether string representation of value should be compact (on one
  line without non-significant whitespace) or use a more human-readable form.

# v0.25.0 2023-11-23

* The json keyword accepts now a left argument; the new dyadic version does the
  encoding, using left argument as optional indent string (for human-readable
  printing). Also, the decoding monadic form has now an improved handling of
  null.
* Add `i r\y` form allowing to specify a maximal number of split results.
* More tolerant csv parsing of double-quotes in non-quoted fields.
* New `mkdir`, `remove`, `rename`, and `stat` IO primitives.
* `read` now works on directories too, and returns a dictionary
  `"name""dir"!(S;I)` with the names of the entries along a boolean array with
  1s for directory entries, and 0s for other kinds of files. Also, read can now
  take a list of filenames and read all of them.
* The `open` IO primitive now only accepts `"r"`, `"w"` and `"a"` modes, that
  is either read-only or write-only. The read-write modes weren't very useful
  unless other primitives were added (like seek and truncate), but the kind of
  problems those are used for are too low-level anyway, not the kind of thing
  you would usually use Goal for.
* Multi-line regexps now ignore leading and trailing whitespace in each line.
  Also, they support comments, either with `/` or `#` (if regexp delimiter is
  already `/`) following a space, similarly as in normal Goal code.
* Remove `rt.prec`, as it's no longer very useful since sprintf-like formatting
  was implemented, and it could make `$s` return non-unique representations for
  floats (breaking change).

# v0.24.0 2023-11-10

This release includes some Go API changes, in order to make all kinds of
extensions possible, including creating new kinds of callable values, carrying
arbitrary Go values into the execution context for use in user-defined
variadics, and a simplification of memory-reuse handling.  This is an important
step towards a stable Go public API for embedding and extending the language.

* New `s!s` fields form that splits the right argument on any of the left
  arguments characters; means `!s` if left argument is the empty string.
* Replicate `f#y` allows negative integers in `f[y]`, to be consistent with
  where `&`.
* Optimize `&d` for numerical values.
* Branchless replicate and weed out for list of booleans.
* Quoting constructs now disallow `'` as a delimiter: there are already enough
  of them (all verb symbols and `/`), and `'` could be used with monadic verb
  `rx`, so avoid surprising need for parens.
* Allow partial application of adverbs to form a derived verb.
* New goal2html program under `cmd/`, similar to `examples/colorize.goal`, but
  using the new scanner from public API.
* Fix a couple of badly formatted error messages.
* Fix `~A` not returning a canonical result on lists of mixed numbers and
  strings.
* Fix handling of `[` right after `:` (would be interpreted as assignment even
  when there were no spaces).
* Fix multi-line comment handling at the beginning of the file (it would accept
  spaces before the first `/` due to them being discarded).
* Go API: new `Get` and `Set` methods for `Context` that help carry values for
  use by user-defined variadics. Rename debug info method `Show` into `String`,
  and fix inconsistent argument order in Compile.
* Go API: new `Callable` interface for making user-defined boxed values
  callable. Also, `Apply` was renamed into `ApplyAt`, `ApplyN` into `Apply`,
  and together with `Apply2` they got revamped into methods for `V` instead of
  `*Context` (minor breaking API change).
* Go API: RegisterMonad and RegisterDyad now allow to redefine existing
  keywords and symbols, as well as to register new symbols, not only keywords
  as before.
* Go API: simplify array indexing: rename `VAt` into `At` and remove the old
  `At` now mostly obsolete due to field `Slice` being exported. Also, remove
  redundant Canonical function, as NewAV normalizes arrays already. Add
  KeyArray and ValueArray methods for dicts, and NewArray function, producing
  Array values instead of generic values, for convenience.
* Go API: unexport `RefCounter` interface, which was a bit low-level, and
  replace it with a `Reusable` method which together with `MarkImmutable` is
  more useful and simpler to understand. Also, export the underlying array
  slice as a field `Slice`, instead of as a method, to allow replacing only the
  underlying slice in the case the array reusable, for example with append.
  This represents some minor breaking API changes. 
* Go API: move scanner into separate package “scan”, and add optional support
  for comment tokens.

# v0.23.0 2023-10-25

* Added case `I'` adverbial form that allows to pick successive values from
  multiple arrays based on a list of indices.
* Recognize and optimize monadic idioms `++`, `*|`, `*<`, and `*>`.
* Optimize monadic use of `:/` (same as last `*|`).
* Fix a couple of outdated examples in Help.
* Make incomplete assignment in sub-expression return a proper syntax error.

# v0.22.0 2023-10-20

* time can now parse an unix time in a custom location, so that you can format
  an unix time in locations other than UTC (the default).
* import does not search `GOALLIB` anymore if the extension is provided in the
  name: this way, it's easy to know, when we're importing a file, whether it's
  a path relative to current directory or relative to `GOALLIB`.
* `f^y` and `f#y` now accept generic empty `f y` for empty `y`.
* Rename runtime info functions from rt.vars into rt.get, because it can do
  some development debug things in addition to the documented features, and
  the previous name doesn't fit all the usages (minor breaking change).
* Make `goal -q` never output anything on stdout; it only suppressed echo
  previously, but not the prompt itself.
* Add `goal -version` option that prints build info.
* Go API: make cmd/Cmd return an error, instead of exiting directly, to make it
  possible to do some cleaning before exiting in case of error.
* Improve a couple error messages.

# v0.21.0 2023-09-20

* New feature: simple debug logging with non-adverbial `\expr` or equivalent
  `rt.log`.
* Add “try in the browser” wasm REPL.

# v0.20.0 2023-06-09

* Format floating point integer values with a trailing `.0`, so that the
  numeric type can be retrieved if parsed again.
* Fix stability of `>X` and `>d`.
* Fix unhandled lone `*` in deep amend, like in `.[x;*;y;z]`.
* Fix ascending flag preservation for `I+i`, `i+I`, and `I-i` in case of
  integer overflow by checking that first element is still smaller than last.

# v0.19.0 2023-06-01

* Flip `+x` now extends array elements (like in take `i#`) to maximum length if
  needed, so that it works with any kind of ragged array.
* There were a few changes in type names in the Go library interface, for
  better consistency, like renaming `Value` into `BV` (boxed value) for
  consistency with `V` (unboxed or boxed value), and `D` for dicts. Also, the
  Array interface is now public.
* Simplification of reference count system, so that it's less error-prone and
  easier to maintain. Because of the GC, we use it only for optimization
  purposes, so we can take advantage of that. We limit reference counting to
  the first level of nesting of generic arrays, marking deeply nested data as
  definitively immutable. This avoids the need for pointers, and simplifies
  handling of shared data. It makes incrementing and decrementing reference
  counts cheaper in the common cases, and most of the time doesn't affect
  negatively performance, except when making many small amends to nested data.
* Various other code refactorings that should facilitate maintenance in the
  long run.

# v0.18.0 2023-05-21

* Improve `d op d` semantics for uncommon or duplicate keys, so that it's in
  line with amend dict.
* Support regexp projections (like for any function).
* Fix regression refcount bug in converges `f\x`.
* Fix refcount bug for out of bounds dict indexing.
* Optimize seeded `x op/y` and `x op\y` for various common op (only non-seeded
  variants had special code before), as well as `~'` and `,//`.
* Optimize small-range computation for sorted inputs in search functions.
* Added some debug and dev purpose tools for refcounting issues and stack
  handling.

# v0.17.1 2023-05-16

* Fix CRLF handling in Goal scripts.

# v0.17.0 2023-05-14

* Rename weed out to `f^y`, related to `X^y`, in the same way that `f#y` is
  related to `X#y`. (breaking change) Now `f_y` is “cut where”, same as `(&f
  y)_y`, but `f` has to return an array of integers.
* Rename `ceil` into `uc`, which can be read both as upper/ceil (for both of
  its meanings on strings and numbers), or just upper case (like `uc` in Perl).
  It felt unnatural to have a name representing only one of its meanings, but
  it was natural to have a single built-in for both (like for `_`), hence a
  name with double-reading. (breaking change)
* Now where `&` allows negative inputs, and simply treats them as zero.
* Allow referencing main namespace from an imported file using `main.` as
  prefix (still thinking about alternative prefixes, like just `m.`, but this
  shouldn't come often so a longer form might be better).
* Implement dyadic version for shell too, and make it inherit STDIN too. It
  works now exactly like run, but through /bin/sh.
* Optimize group by for sorted indices, and `X?Y` (find) and `X¿Y` (in) for
  long generic arrays too (hashing).
* Make `f'[d;y;…]` and `f\[x;d;z;…]` return dictionary too in n-arg case.
* Fix syntax regression when projecting `@` due to missing check for dyadic
  case when optimizing away `@` and replacing it with a single opcode.
* Fix bug in `s?r` when there is no match: it returned
  (start-offset;end-offset) instead of (offset;len) in such case.
* Fix refcount bug in each and scan adverbs when function returned a mutated
  global.

# v0.16.0 2023-05-05

* Make out-indexing valid and return the zero value of the array or dict, in
  the same way as padding does (0s for numeric arrays, empty strings for string
  arrays, and zero value based on first element type for generic arrays, or
  an empty generic array if it's empty). In particular, outdexing results
  returned by group will return an empty array as expected.
* Now that `X@i` does pad on outdexing, invert `i@Y` and `i#Y` swap from
  previous release to keep more compatibility with K. It's also now quite
  natural that `i@Y` is the same as `Y@!i` (except for being more efficient by
  not actually generating indices). Also, new mnemonic: `@` looks like a bit
  like a zero, so it pads.
* Make `i!n` mod/div, and remove `mod` keyword, both for better compatibility
  with ngn/k, and because only `i!I` is easy to vectorize (for example for
  powers of two, and to produce a result with smaller type for small i). As a
  result, cut shape is now `i$y` (used in `J` too for reshape), and string
  padding is done with `i!s` (though it can be done too with new sprintf-like
  format `s$y`).  Also, span `i$i` replaces range `i!i`, which was not very
  composable (albeit convenient). (breaking changes)
* New format `s$y` form that provides classic sprintf-like functionality, for
  when more advanced formatting than just space padding is useful. Formatting
  works element-wise when `s` contains a single formatting word, like `"%03d"`,
  and list-wise when it contains more, like `"%s=%.4f"` (expecting `2~#y`).
* New `"b"$s` for converting a string to and from array of bytes.
* New `"c"$s` for converting a string to and from array of code points, and make
  old `"i"$s` now just be parse/cast to int, and `"n"$s` only parse/cast to
  number (floats).
* New `"s"$y` form that formats in a default way non-strings element-wise,
  instead of just the whole `y` like in `$y`. Also, it leaves strings as-is,
  unlike `$y` which quotes them with escapes.
* Return `"i"` for `@i`, not `"n"`, because integers and floats are different
  types, even though implicit conversions are made when possible.
* New `0i` value, representing the minimum representable integer. It's used in
  `"i"$s` when parsing an integer with invalid syntax, as well as in the
  special shortcut `0i?Y` for doing a shuffle. We use `0i` for consistency,
  instead of `0N`, because `i` is the name of the integer type.
* `$X` returns now stranding representation for mixed lists of strings and
  numbers, without parens.
* Add `¿` as symbol alternative for in and firsts, the boolean primitive
  counterparts of `?`.
* Rename `atan2` into `atan`, which now accepts either one or two arguments
  (same simplification as Lua 5.3 did). (breaking change)
* More consistent results in `op/x` for empty list `x`. Now we use the default
  zero value for the given list type, except for a few special reductions where
  a different neutral element is clear (like `*/`, `&/`, and `|/` for
  non-generic numeric lists).
* Make `X#d` follow same semantics as `X^d` (except for being the negation
  of it), returning a dictionary derived from `d`, preserving duplicate keys,
  but with keys not in `X` removed. In particular, it does not add new keys to
  `d` anymore, so dictionary padding should either be done with merge or
  individually to its arrays.
* Implement !i for negative integers too.
* Improvements in sorting of integers, depending on the range, using either
  counting sort (`^I` for small-range) or radix sort (for `^I`, `<I`, and
  `>I` when `I` fits into a `[]int8`, `[]int16` or `[]int32` slice).
* Arrays of small integers (0-255) are now represented as arrays of bytes,
  saving memory (in particular when converting a string to bytes, or even
  codepoints if the string is ASCII), and facilitating small-range
  optimizations for searching and sorting. Previously, only booleans where
  stored more compactly.
* Recognize `x:op x` assignment as potential in-place operation for global
  variables too (previously only `x op:y` form was recognized for global
  variables).
* Fix missing integer overflow check in odometer, a regression in boolean
  grade (maybe posterior to 0.15.0), as well as other minor issues.

# v0.15.0 2023-04-21

This release makes quite a few significant changes and improvements.

* Rename `bytes s` into `&s`, because getting the length in bytes of a string
  is quite a fundamental operation, even if it's not used that often (breaking
  change).
* New take/repeat `i@y` equivalent to old `i#y`, that now is take/pad. Both give
  same results unless `i>#y` or `(-i)>#y`. A simple way to pad arrays with
  zero-values (now properly based on first element type, or default type) was
  missing.  `@` in kind of a circle, which is a good mnemonic for the cyclic
  behavior (which also feels to me more like an apply action than just padding
  would). Also, because new `X#d` does padding for new keys, it's expected that
  `i#y` does too for out of bound indices. (breaking change: Actually `i#y`
  swapped to K normal behavior in next release, so that `i@y` does padding)
* Make `i^Y`, `i^s`, `i!s`, `i!Y` use `i` as the length of the result, and use
  `-i` for the old behavior (breaking change). This was suggested by @Marshall
  on the aplfarm matrix channel.
* Make `=I` return index-counting `#'=I`, because the former is not used often
  in this form, and can be obtained with group keys `=(!#I)!I` and group by
  `{!#x}=I`. (minor breaking change)
* Improve state of things with fill/pad values of generic arrays: now we use
  the type of the first element to determine the zero value if it's not empty,
  and we use () otherwise (which is often the desired default for generic
  arrays). Previously fills where only really usable in numeric and string
  arrays.
* Rename fields from v0.13 into `!s`, and add new `=s` lines (like `"\n"\` but
  handles `"\r\n"` endings too). The mnemonics for the new name is that fields
  is mainly used to break text vertically, while `=s` only breaks it
  horizontally (and `=` represents two lines).  (breaking change)
* Rename utf8.valid into utf8, and remove utf8.rcount, because it's the same as
  `-1+""#x` with same underlying counting code. (breaking change)
* Remove delete `X_i` and `s_i`, because they don't follow the common pattern,
  are not that useful (outside of golfing maybe), and `_` is already quite
  polysemic. (minor breaking change)
* Implement w/o keys `X^d` and w/ keys `X#d`.
* Implement `+d` as swap of keys and values. The reason for this is that Goal
  does not have tables, and they are not planned, as making them useful would
  require a lot of work (including some kind of query methods).
* Implement `d.y` for `1<#y`, and `X@d`.
* New `.X` self-dict form, equivalent to `{x!x}`.
* New `-s` form trimming trailing spaces, as defined by Unicode.
* Implement `@[f1;x;f2]`, like `.[f1;y;f2]` but doing `f1@x` instead of `f1 .
  y`.
* Improve at depth indexing of mixed dicts and arrays.
* `<d` and `>d` return now sorted dicts, instead of just the keys, and `^d`
  sorts `d` by its keys.
* Fix default rank of `s/` `s\` `I/` `I\` (used in the case they would be
  followed by a fold or scan, which would be quite rare).
* When an in-place assignment operation panics, clear the variable (instead of
  producing random garbage).

# v0.14.0 2023-04-08

* New `?(-i)` form returning normal distribution.
* Make rt.ofs and rt.prec return the previous value.
* New -q command-line option disabling echo.
* New examples/ directory with some example scripts.
* csv now accepts non-string fields (it stringifies fields if necessary).
* Do not search for script filename when -e option is provided.
* Fix possible refcount bug with shallowClone and join of generic array.

# v0.13.0 2023-04-03

* New rt.ofs runtime builtin for setting the output field separator for string
  lists used in print S and "$S", defaulting to space.
* Export OFS and Prec parameters in Context API.
* Allow use of 3-arg ? as function too, by putting parens around, in which
  case, the arguments are evaluated like for any function (this can be useful
  in special cases where avoiding branching improves liveness analysis and
  performance).
* Make the new `=s` form of last release work with the `#'=x` special case.
* Fixed incorrect newline termination in x say S form.

# v0.12.0 2023-04-02

* New `=s` fields form, similar to `rx/[\n \t]+/\` but splits on any kind of unicode
  space.
* New "zone" command for time.
* Simplify math builtins: atan2 in place of acos, asin, atan, and remove tan
  (provide same functions as AWK).

# v0.11.0 2023-03-30

* New `i!i` range form.
* New `""^s` unicode-aware trim spaces form.
* New `i?Y` and `(-i)?Y` forms.
* New `x utf8.valid s` form for replacing invalid byte sequences.
* New `i?Y` roll array and `(-i)?Y` deal array forms.
* More permissive projection application: for example `+[][2;3]` is valid, even
  though `+[]` has rank 1 when used in adverbial contexts that make use of
  function rank.
* Disallow space before adverb application. For `'` this means that usage is
  reserved for early return on error, and for `\` it has no meaning yet.
* For consistency, make run s form return its standard output too, and return
  a dictionary in error case containing exit code, message and output.
* More consistent error messages.
* Fix some unhandled cases of `.s` with lambda return.

# v0.10.0 2023-03-26

* Renamings and cleanups in the library interface, preparing for a stable
  and documented API.
* Rename goal builtin into separate rt.CMD builtins.
* Improvements in import builtin supporting GOALLIB environment variable,
  both use of extension or not, and importing several files at once.
* Improvements and fixes in help, with better examples and a new short FAQ.
* Improvements in REPL handling of multi-line quoting constructs.
* The json builtin can now handle several JSON strings at once.
* Error location improvements in value application.
* Fix panic-case handling in eval, in particular error location.

# v0.9.0 2023-03-23

* New json builtin for parsing JSON strings.
* New chdir builtin for changing working directory.
* Implement i!s colsplit form for strings.
* New `goal["time";s;n]` and `goal["time";f;x;n]` forms for timing code.
* New `d[]` form equivalent to `.d` (for dicts).
* New help feature: extract help for specific op.
* Fixed refcount bug in `i f\y` form.
* More tests, and various refactorings, and documentation improvements.

# v0.8.0 2023-03-13

* lists `(expr1;expr2)` are now evaluated from left to right. This avoids a list
  reversal in the implementation, and is also more intuitive in multi-line
  lists. Function arguments in binary and index application are still evaluated
  from right to left as always.  Now lists and sequences are similar, except
  that the first construct collects all values, and the second returns the last
  one only.
* In `rq//` raw quoting introduced in last release, allow escaping delimiter by
  doubling it, as a simplification of previous rule. Note that the old
  backquoted raw strings behave the same as always and do not have any way of
  writing a literal backquote.
* `,/()` now returns ()
* `"n"$y` returns 0n instead of error for incorrect syntax, as it is more
  convenient by ensuring a numerical result.
* Various bug fixes and more op/ special code.

# v0.7.0 2023-03-02

Highlights:

* String interpolation in "" strings, as well as the new `qq//` Perl-style
  quoting form with custom delimiter (potentially breaking if strings contained
  character `$`, which now needs to be escaped).
* New `rq//` quoting form with custom delimiter for raw strings. Allow custom
  delimiter for `rx//` form too.
* New x run s form, piping string x to command s, and returning its own stdout.
* Optimize `#'=` so that icount can be finally removed.
* Various small improvements and fixes in language's help.

# v0.6.0 2023-02-26

This release has various breaking changes in the core language.  They should be
more rare from now on (but still possible if important until we reach 1.0), and
they will at least be documented.  Some changes might still happen in the
embedding API.

Highlights:

* General IO with open (including pipes), read, close, flush, and env builtins,
  as well as STDIN, STDOUT, STDERR globals containing the standard filehandles.
* slurp s became read s, complementing the new read h form.
* New “run” builtin for running commands without shell.
* Dict support is now implemented in all builtins where it makes sense (though
  the help only mentions most interesting cases).
* New forms `x_i` and `s_i` (delete)
* `i$s` is now pad, and `i!x` is the old `i$s`.
* Added special code for some `op\` and `op'` forms.
* Many improvements in help.
* Added goal builtin for runtime state inspection and configuration, like
  floating point formatting precision. Also, the seed builtin was removed, and
  uses the goal builtin with a "seed" argument.
* Added aliases « and » for shift and rshift.

# Credits.md

Source: https://github.com/wrnrlr/goal-mirror/blob/master/Credits.md

Goal made use of many inspirations sources both for design and implementation.

Language design was greatly inspired by both K (for syntax and many
primitives), in particular the [ngn/k](https://codeberg.org/ngn/k) dialect, and
[BQN](https://mlochbaum.github.io/BQN/index.html) (a few fundamental primitives
like group by, classify and shifts). I was thinking of Perl and Raku when
adding regexp literals, quoting constructs, and a couple of IO primitives.
There is some inspiration from the implementation language, Go: similar syntax
for numbers, string literals, and time layouts.

I wrote the bytecode implementation after reading the one for
[GoAWK](https://benhoyt.com/writings/goawk/), and it still shows. I wrote the
scanner after reading [ivy's](https://pkg.go.dev/robpike.io/ivy). Vim syntax
highlighting is based on [ngn/k's](https://codeberg.org/ngn/k).

Be sure to check out all those great projects if you haven't yet!
